items.title: Amazon's Push to Dominate Black Friday With All-Day Sports
items.summary: Amazon planned a 15-hour run of live events on Black Friday: golf's The Skins Game, its fourth NFL Black Friday game (Broncos v Steelers) and an NBA doubleheader including the Knicks against the Spurs. The sports content sits in front of the paywall, so no subscription or Prime membership is needed. Last year's Black Friday NFL game averaged 16.33 million viewers, up 21% on 2024 and 70% on the first game in 2023, and Amazon sports partnerships head Charlie Neiman said the company wants big exclusive events that matter to a large share of the Prime base, with more golf rights possible 'if it's big enough'.
items.what_it_means: Streamers are turning holidays into owned, free-to-watch sports days built around their commercial calendar.

items.title: Gloucestershire County Cricket Club unveils new 'Bristol Lions' identity to compete in T20 Blast for 2027
items.summary: Gloucestershire County Cricket Club has launched Bristol Lions as a separate T20 identity for its men's and women's teams from the 2027 season, while County Championship and One-Day Cup cricket stays under the Gloucestershire name. The club says the brand came from audience research, market insight and commercial analysis and is meant to reach Bristol sports followers who have not engaged with county cricket. Head of audience development Jenny Hall said the identity allows a step change in ticketing, partnership and commercial potential. This is a club announcement published in SportsPro's announcements section.
items.what_it_means: A heritage club is creating a second, city-facing brand to recruit fans its existing identity was not reaching.

items.title: DEAG lifts nine-month revenue while EBITDA falls 27%
items.summary: German promoter DEAG grew revenue 4.3% to EUR336.8m in the first nine months of 2026, while EBITDA fell 27% to EUR13.8m. It put the profit pressure partly down to developing new event formats and investing in digitalisation and automation, particularly in ticketing. DEAG sold 9.6m tickets in the period, most through its own platforms such as myticket and gigantic.com, and is continuing a buy-and-build strategy after being acquired by Enhanced Group earlier in November.
items.what_it_means: A mid-size promoter is paying now to own its ticketing and new formats, and margins are carrying the cost.

items.title: How the WNBA's First Union Chief Sees Its Billion-Dollar Growth
items.summary: Coquese Washington, the first WNBPA president, told FOS the new collective bargaining agreement fulfils the union's 1998 goal of making the WNBA a full career. Players once earned as little as $15,000 and her first CBA in 1999 lifted the minimum to $25,000; the March deal raises it to $270,000, and the league says it will pay players more than $1 billion in salary through 2032. Washington credits recent metrics showing the league is a viable business, and the piece notes few players now need to play overseas, with offseason leagues like Unrivaled keeping many in the US year-round.
items.what_it_means: Women's basketball is now built on commercial proof points, where early deals relied on belief.

items.title: Auckland to establish four-stadium 'coordinated' network
items.summary: Auckland Council has unanimously approved a Stadium Network Investment Plan that groups the city's four stadiums into a coordinated network, assigning each a role and directing events to the 'venue of best fit'. Eden Park keeps its own governance and its role as the international concert host, with approval for 32 concerts a year, while the upgraded Western Springs Bowl takes a music-first focus and Go Media Stadium and North Harbour Stadium act as sporting hubs. The council says the aim is to strengthen event hosting amid financial pressures.
items.what_it_means: Cities under financial pressure are planning venues as one portfolio and dividing up the event calendar between them.

items.title: Gridiron gridlock: NFL calls shots on US rights spending
items.summary: The SportBusiness Podcast episode covers the big streamers' appetite for sports rights, with the NFL's next domestic contracts described as shaping media companies' decisions while Fifa's US World Cup rights auction continues. It also covers BT's Euro 2028 national sponsorship, which lets it partially keep Wembley branding rights in a departure from the usual clean-site policy, and asks whether Uefa is relaxing its stance on stadium naming rights. This summary is drawn from the episode page only.
items.what_it_means: The NFL's coming renewal is setting the pace for every other US rights negotiation.

items.title: Bodø/Glimt lead global football clubs with 555 per cent social media growth in 2026
items.summary: Football Benchmark data shows Bodø/Glimt grew their combined Instagram and TikTok following from about 136,000 to 888,000 between 1 January and 17 November 2026, a 555% rise and the fastest among leading clubs. Chicago Fire FC were second at 205% and Trabzonspor third at 140%. The release links the growth to the Norwegian club's Champions League run, including wins over Manchester City and Atletico de Madrid. It is an agency announcement from Empower Sports published in SportsPro's announcements section.
items.what_it_means: A big competition run can build a small club an international audience fast, which it then has to turn into something commercial.

items.title: Michael Redd: College Football Is the Next Frontier for Team Ownership
items.summary: NBA All-Star turned investor Michael Redd told FOS's Portfolio Players he sees more ownership potential in college football than the NFL, because there are 32 NFL teams but 300-plus college programmes. Deals so far are mostly minority stakes and private credit, such as Utah's deal with Otro Capital and the Big 12's agreement with RedBird Capital Partners. Redd also expects bigger media rights paydays, suggesting the SEC and Big Ten could form their own super league that would attract streamers like Amazon and Netflix.
items.what_it_means: Private capital is looking at college sport as the next ownership market as pro franchise prices climb.
